name: delegate
description:
Delegate a task to a different identity tier.

Use this to assign work to a tier whose specialty matches the task. Provide a clear task description so the receiving tier has full context.

Semantics:
- Creates a FRESH child context loaded with the target tier's full system prompt (identity + constitution + tools).
- Child context does NOT inherit the parent's conversation history.
- Filesystem state is shared with the parent by default (`delegation.isolation: none`): the child's edits land in the project directly. When the engine is configured with `delegation.isolation: sandbox`, the child instead runs in a copy of the project and its edits come back to the consumer as a patch — nothing it writes reaches the project until the consumer applies that patch.
- The child's final result is returned to the lead context as a `[DELEGATION COMPLETE: <tier>] <summary>` user message for re-synthesis.
- If the active tier has `relay_single_delegate` configured, the child's result is auto-relayed to the parent without re-synthesis. The child can also signal `coverage_gap=true` via entropic.complete to SUPPRESS the auto-relay (the lead then receives a [COVERAGE GAP] message instead, with `gap_description` and `suggested_files`, and may chain to a follow-up specialist). #10 v2.1.4.

The available tiers are listed in the `target` enum. Choose based on the tier whose specialty matches the work that needs to be done.

Context seeding (gh#162, v2.13.0): pass `context` with every file path you already located. The child receives them as an opening [CONTEXT] block of references and opens them itself — nothing is inlined, so this costs the child almost nothing and saves it a rediscovery pass. A tier configured with `requires_context: true` REFUSES a delegation that carries none.

target.description: Target identity tier to delegate to

task.description: Natural language description of the task to delegate

max_turns.description: Maximum number of turns the delegate can use (optional). The child's loop stops at this many iterations and hands back whatever it has produced so far, marked partial. It can only TIGHTEN the limit the operator configured for that tier — a value larger than the tier's own bound leaves that bound in place. Omit it unless the task genuinely has a small, known turn budget.

context.description: Files you ALREADY know are relevant, passed to the child as references it can open directly. Use this whenever you have a path from earlier work — a child that has to re-find it may not, and may answer from guesswork instead.

path.description: File path the child should read

note.description: Optional one-line reason this file matters
